question: Does later departure phase predict shorter stopover use within the same animal after accounting for common year effects?
missingness: 25 original BBMM-quality exclusions are missing, never zero-imputed
primary_sample: complete cases belonging to animals observed in at least two distinct source years
exposure: DFP_Start in days; positive means later relative to the annual winter-range green-up peak
outcome: stopover.day; observed whole-journey stopover duration, including genuine zeros
primary_model: stopover_it = animal_fixed_intercept_i + year_fixed_intercept_t + beta * DFP_Start_it + error_it
primary_estimand: common linear within-animal association conditional on observed year effects, days of stopover per phase day
reference_sample: identical to the primary repeated-animal complete-case sample

uncertainty.method: paired animal-cluster percentile bootstrap; all observations of each drawn animal retained; duplicated draws relabeled; all fixed effects refitted
uncertainty.scope: conditional on the observed years, not a population-of-years interval

sensitivity: omit every source year in turn, reselect repeated complete-case animals and refit if mathematically identifiable; report every outcome
prior_art: Ortega 2023 already reports compensation and animal/year random-intercept models; this tests robustness to unrestricted fixed animal intercepts, not the first individual-adjusted analysis
claim_limit: conditional within-animal time-allocation association, not causal information use, learning, remaining actionability, fitness, or independent biological replication
rejected_design: arrival-phase prediction augmented by whole-journey speed was rejected before fitting because speed is distance divided by arrival-minus-departure time; holdout does not remove this arithmetic and temporal overlap
